newsitem.title: USA: Senator urges US defer aid to China shipping firm.
newsitem.headline: Senator urges US defer aid to China shipping firm.

text.p: Senator John McCain on Wednesday urged the Transportation and Defense departments to hold up any benefits to Chinese Ocean Shipping Co (COSCO) until the completion of an investigation into its pricing practices.

The chairman of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee cited comments to the panel on March 20 by Harold Creel, chairman of the Federal Maritime Commission, that COSCO was engaged in allegedly unfair pricing activities.
McCain, an Arizona Republican, said Creel told him that a commission investigation into unfair pricing by COSCO should completed in a few weeks.

COSCO, owned and operated by the Chinese government, is due to receive federal loan guarantees to build ships in Alabama, as well as to receive property in Long Beach, Calif., for a terminal facility, the senator said.
"The administration should put on hold any action that would assist COSCO until we learn whether the company is unfairly competing against U.S. carriers," McCain said.
He added that "I firmly believe in free trade, but taxpayers should not be asked to subsidize unfair foreign competition."
